statement: The function $f(x)=x^2-4x+3$ is defined for $x\ge2$. Find $f^{-1}(x)$, stating its domain and range.
solution:
Completing the square, $f(x)=(x-2)^2-1$. For $x\ge2$ this is increasing, with minimum $-1$ at $x=2$, so the range of $f$ is $[-1,\infty)$.

Set $y=(x-2)^2-1$. Since $x\ge2$, $x-2=\sqrt{y+1}$ (the positive root). Hence $x=2+\sqrt{y+1}$, and
$$f^{-1}(x)=2+\sqrt{x+1}.$$
The domain of $f^{-1}$ is the range of $f$, namely $[-1,\infty)$; its range is $[2,\infty)$ (the domain of $f$).
